Subject: Session-level learning toggle and prompt provenance for pilot

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the latency looks promising. Before we sign up our pilot, Legal and Product have a couple of specific asks tied to how interactions with the model are handled:

1) Per-customer/session learning toggle: we need a contractable guarantee that certain sessions (flagged by our app) will not be used for model improvement or offline training. Ideally this is enforced at request time (a header or metadata flag) and logged for audit.

2) Prompt provenance: we want an audit trail so that every response can be traced to the request session id and a short provenance header (who/which product sent it). This will help with incident triage and exportability.

3) Derivative handling: if there are aggregated telemetry or derivative datasets (for ops), they must be pseudonymized and cannot include prompt text for opted-out sessions.

4) Cross-border transfer: CareLane serves EU customers; any transfer of content outside the EU needs to be explicit in the DPA and we may require a proxy/onshore processing lane.

Can you share sample contract language or an addendum we can review? Also: timing — we hoped to get contractual sign-off within two weeks for an early June pilot.

Attaching our internal checklist for context.

Regards,
Sanjay Mehta
Head of Product, CareLane

Subject: Re: Session-level learning toggle and prompt provenance for pilot

Hi Sanjay —

Really appreciate the clear asks. Short answer: we can support a request-level "learning toggle" and supply provenance headers, and we can propose DPA addendum language to make this contractual. High-level plan below; attaching a short spec and a redline we can start from.

Proposed approach (ops + legal):
- Request header: X-Redwood-Learning: opt-out|opt-in (default opt-in). When set to opt-out, the runtime will:
  * mark the request as non-learning in the trace and persist the flag in the audit log
  * exclude raw prompt text from any internal telemetry captures destined for model improvement pipelines
  * keep a lightweight provenance record (session id, tenant id, timestamp, agent id) for 30 days for incident triage (no raw prompt text)
- Pseudonymous telemetry: aggregated metrics (latency, token counts, error rates) allowed for opt-out sessions but with prompt text redaction.
- Cross-border: provide an onshore processing lane (EU region) and, if needed, a proxy path that prevents egress of opted-out content from the EU. This will be surfaced in the DPA with options (onshore KMS or regional processing).
- Contract language: suggest a 1-page addendum that references the DPA, defines "opt-out sessions", requires Redwood to maintain audit logs and provide monthly attestation for the pilot period.

Next steps:
1) Kimberly — can Legal review the attached redline and flag anything we should tighten?
2) Sanjay — if your team agrees, we can send a DocuSign addendum by EOD tomorrow and schedule a short technical handoff for next week.

Attaching: session_toggle_spec.xlsx, carelane_dpa_redline_v1.pdf

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Exec — Enterprise Health
Redwood Inference

Attachments: session_toggle_spec.xlsx (spec stub), carelane_dpa_redline_v1.pdf (redline stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Aditya — forwarding suggested legal edits inline (see redline). Key points for negotiation and operationalization: 

1) Precise clause for "no-model-improvement": replace loose phrasing with: "Redwood shall not use Customer Data from Opt-Out Sessions for training, fine-tuning, or improvement of any model; 'use' excludes aggregated telemetry as expressly permitted in Section 3."

2) Subprocessors and proof of non-use: we need a subprocessor mapping clause and a 'proofflow' obligation for the pilot — Redwood should be able to provide evidence (audit log snapshot plus KMS access traces) within 10 business days on request.

3) Prompt provenance retention: limit the stored provenance metadata to 30 days by default for Opt-Out Sessions. If CareLane requests longer retention, it must be contractual and justified for compliance reasons.

4) Cross-border controls: propose enumerated options in the DPA (a) EU-only processing, (b) EU processing + temporary onshore transit with logging, (c) EU processing + customer-managed KMS. For (b) add a requirement that transient copies are not used for model improvement and are deleted within a 72-hour window.

5) Derivatives and telemetry: require that any derivative dataset excludes raw prompts for Opt-Out Sessions and be pseudonymized. Recommend adding an operational SLA for redaction (e.g., within 48 hours of ingestion).

6) Compliance evidence: suggest clause for quarterly attestation during the first 12 months of the contract and a right to audit (with notice and scoping).

I'll attach a redlined DPA (I edited the addendum Aditya shared). Once Sanjay confirms the approach, we can route the redline to CareLane legal and prepare the DocuSign package.

- Kimberly
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
